title: donoteat this BONUS EPISODE 1: Black Wall Street
premise: The presenter traces Greenwood’s locally circulating wealth, the 1921 racist massacre and its recovery, arguing that later freeway and institutional redevelopment did more lasting damage by removing land from community use. He ties together racism, class power and community self-defense, and argues that prosperity offered no protection.
coverage: Greenwood’s prosperity, the racist massacre, rebuilding and later displacement by a freeway and campus, through the credits. The violence is narrated and illustrated with photographs and game scenes, not reenacted by historical characters. Historical claims are the presenter’s account.

panels.heading: First free bonus episode
panels.description: The circular DNE/ONE FARE emblem sits on black as the presenter introduces the Patreon-funded history series.
panels.camera: Static emblem on black.
panels.action: The emblem holds while the presenter speaks.

panels.heading: CW double meaning
panels.description: The green THE CW television-network logo replaces the emblem just as the narrator introduces a content warning.
panels.camera: Hard cut from the emblem to the logo.
panels.visualGag: The content-warning abbreviation CW is literalized as the television network logo; the following list resolves the ambiguity.

panels.heading: Content warning payoff
panels.description: White MURDER, MOB VIOLENCE, RACISM, THE KLAN, BAD POLICE WORK and RAPE IS MENTIONED lines build on black.
panels.camera: Static text card on black.
panels.action: The warning lines build one after another.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the preceding CW-network logo: this is a serious content warning, not a TV-network announcement.

panels.heading: Tulsa skyline
panels.description: A color photograph presents Tulsa downtown towers.
panels.camera: Static photograph.

panels.heading: Art Deco context
panels.description: A monumental gray Art Deco church is shown during the architectural survey.
panels.camera: Static photograph.

panels.heading: Oral Roberts campus
panels.description: A gold geometric building introduces the campus montage; a spired circular structure follows.
panels.camera: Cuts between two static photographs.

panels.heading: Tower outside downtown
panels.description: A close tower view accompanies the tallest-building claim.
panels.camera: Static close photograph of the tower.

panels.heading: Prosperous Greenwood
panels.description: A black-and-white commercial street photograph shows storefronts, cars and pedestrians.
panels.camera: Static archival photograph.
panels.action: The street scene is a still image.

panels.heading: Black Wall Street named
panels.description: White BLACK WALL STREET text isolates the neighborhood name on black.
panels.camera: Static text card on black.

panels.heading: Massacre preview
panels.description: A black-and-white photograph shows a large smoke plume over buildings.
panels.camera: Static archival photograph.
panels.action: The smoke is frozen in the still image.

panels.heading: Limits and a serious register
panels.description: The DNE emblem returns while the presenter explains the limited usefulness of Cities: Skylines for traumatic events and his decision to reduce jokes.
panels.camera: Static emblem on black.
panels.action: The emblem holds while the presenter explains.

panels.heading: O. W. Gurley
panels.description: A seated portrait introduces Gurley and the 1906 purchase.
panels.camera: Static portrait.

panels.heading: Parcel boundaries
panels.description: A red polygon on a satellite map labels Pine Street, Cincinnati Avenue, Lansing Avenue and Frisco railroad tracks.
panels.camera: Static satellite map with a drawn outline.

panels.heading: Frisco never reached Frisco
panels.description: A FRISCO LINES system map replaces the parcel map.
panels.camera: Cut from the parcel map to the railroad map.
panels.visualGag: The railroad map backs up the spoken aside that the St. Louis to San Francisco Railroad never actually reached San Francisco, a dry joke about the name.

panels.heading: Business district emerges
panels.description: The earlier commercial street photograph returns, followed by another historical street view.
panels.camera: Cuts between static street photographs.

panels.heading: Unslumming
panels.description: Jane Jacobs appears holding papers above the quoted word UNSLUMMING.
panels.camera: Static photograph with a caption.

panels.heading: North End comparison
panels.description: A contemporary brick-lined Boston street illustrates the comparison; Jacobs’s book cover follows.
panels.camera: Cut from a street photograph to a book cover.

panels.heading: Past crowding and present vitality
panels.description: A crowded historical street photo contrasts with the subsequent modern brick block.
panels.camera: Cut from a historical photograph to a modern one.

panels.heading: Credit denied
panels.description: A multicolored redlining map accompanies the Federal Housing Administration blacklisting discussion.
panels.camera: Static map.

panels.heading: Recirculation mechanism
panels.description: The emblem holds while narration explains barter, neighborhood banks and residents becoming wealthier in place.
panels.camera: Static emblem on black.
panels.action: The emblem holds through the explanation.

panels.heading: Five bucks becomes a portrait
panels.description: An Abraham Lincoln portrait appears immediately before the hoagie example.
panels.camera: Static portrait.
panels.visualGag: Lincoln stands in for five bucks, invoking the five-dollar bill without showing one, and leads straight into the sandwich purchase.

panels.heading: Spend it at the deli
panels.description: A large sliced hoagie photo replaces Lincoln.
panels.camera: Cut from Lincoln to the sandwich photo.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the Lincoln setup: the five dollars turn into a local sandwich purchase, and the gag becomes a real explanation of how money recirculates.

panels.heading: Suppliers and New Jersey
panels.description: Dietz & Watson branding overlays a map with a thick black arrow; an Amoroso’s map follows.
panels.camera: Static map with a logo overlay, then a second map.
panels.action: The arrow is drawn on the map; nothing moves.
panels.visualGag: The map-and-arrow inserts go with the regional taunt that the suppliers moved to New Jersey because they are cowards.

panels.heading: Amazon leakage
panels.description: A sunglasses-and-vest portrait of Jeff Bezos appears as the narrator describes purchases from Amazon disappearing into an untaxed hole.
panels.camera: Static portrait.
panels.visualGag: The cutaway gives the abstract untaxed hole Bezos's face, and leads into the chain-store and Patreon examples of money leaking away.

panels.heading: Chain-store alternative
panels.description: A Wawa storefront photo cuts to a circled map location.
panels.camera: Cut from a storefront photo to a map.
panels.visualGag: The money-leakage comparison continues and sets up the narrator's admission that his own Patreon also pulls dollars out of the neighborhood.

panels.heading: Patreon incriminates itself
panels.description: A screenshot of the donoteat Patreon page appears, with a Franklin preview and a beer image visible.
panels.camera: Static screenshot.
panels.visualGag: Self-own: the narrator's own funding appeal turns out to be one more way money leaves a viewer's neighborhood.

panels.heading: Landlord punchline
panels.description: Mr. Monopoly (Rich Uncle Pennybags), the Monopoly mascot, appears with a cane and a lifted foot.
panels.camera: Static cartoon image.
panels.visualGag: The landlord, last stop in the chain, appears as Monopoly's cartoon capitalist, a visual answer to whatever landlords spend money on.

panels.heading: Gurley and the initial buyers
panels.description: Gurley’s seated portrait returns while the presenter notes that people able to buy his land in 1906 were already relatively well off. The following drinking-fountain image introduces segregation as another factor.
panels.camera: Static portrait, then a cut to the drinking-fountain photograph.

panels.heading: Segregation traps spending
panels.description: A historical photograph of unequal drinking fountains marked WHITE and COLORED illustrates the imposed racial boundary that the presenter says confined shopping to Greenwood.
panels.camera: Static photograph replacing Gurley’s portrait.

panels.heading: Money sink
panels.description: The emblem holds as the presenter describes a dollar circulating repeatedly within Greenwood and the role of resident owners.
panels.camera: Static emblem on black.
panels.action: The emblem holds through the explanation.

panels.heading: Airplane wealthy
panels.description: A static biplane photograph illustrates the claimed private aircraft ownership.
panels.camera: Static photograph.
panels.action: The plane sits still in the photo.

panels.heading: Automobiles and exclusion
panels.description: A historical automobile portrait is followed by the segregated drinking-fountain photograph.
panels.camera: Cut from the automobile portrait to the drinking-fountain photograph.

panels.heading: Explicit disclaimer
panels.description: White TO BE CLEAR: SEGREGATION IS DUMB AND BAD text fills the black screen.
panels.camera: Static text card on black.
panels.visualGag: The blunt, deliberately redundant disclaimer heads off any reading of the prosperity explanation as an endorsement of segregation. It comes back during the recovery discussion.

panels.heading: Reconstructed Greenwood
panels.description: A daytime game aerial shows a street grid, low-rise shops, houses and several rail corridors.
panels.camera: The aerial sweeps around the game city and rises toward an overhead view.
panels.action: The view travels over the intact game city while the narration covers the history.

panels.heading: Reference intersection
panels.description: The game aerial receives ARCHER STREET and GREENWOOD AVENUE labels, then MKT, ATSF and FRISCO RAILROAD labels.
panels.camera: Fixed aerial with labels added in turn.

panels.heading: Present-day reference block
panels.description: A satellite aerial shows the baseball diamond and adjacent freeway in the same area.
panels.camera: Static satellite view.

panels.heading: Interurban connections
panels.description: The reconstructed aerial labels SANDY SPRINGS RR; a regional map names Greenwood, Tulsa and Sandy Springs.
panels.camera: Labeled aerial, then a cut to a regional map.

panels.heading: Shopping streets and houses
panels.description: A closer moving aerial passes warehouses and the commercial strip toward rows of houses.
panels.camera: A closer aerial moves over the warehouses and shops toward the houses.
panels.action: The camera passes over the game city; no people are animated.

panels.heading: Memorial Day
panels.description: A black title card reads MAY 30, 1921 / MEMORIAL DAY.
panels.camera: Static text card on black.

panels.heading: Dick Rowland and the Drexel building
panels.description: The daytime model leads into a historical building photograph, then a modern Street View of the site.
panels.camera: Game aerial, then a cut to a historical photograph and a modern street view.
panels.action: The game city gives way to photographs of the real site.

panels.heading: This one
panels.description: A white THIS ONE arrow on the historical photo identifies the smaller building beside the tall tower.
panels.camera: Static photograph with an arrow overlay.
panels.action: The arrow points to the building.

panels.heading: Uncertain elevator incident
panels.description: The rotating daylight reconstruction plays while the narrator recounts Sarah Page, the scream and the reported incident. The elevator encounter itself is not shown.
panels.camera: The daylight aerial slowly circles the game city.
panels.action: The view rotates over the intact city as the narrator tells the story.

panels.heading: May 31 detention
panels.description: TUESDAY / MAY 31, 1921 appears on a black date card.
panels.camera: Static text card on black.

panels.heading: Inflammatory headline
panels.description: A newspaper clipping reads Nab Negro for Attacking Girl In an Elevator, carrying the presenter’s account of the Tulsa Tribune escalation.
panels.camera: Static newspaper clipping.

panels.heading: Courthouse fortified
panels.description: A static black-and-white photo of the Tulsa County Courthouse represents Sheriff McCullough’s defensive preparations.
panels.camera: Static archival photograph.

panels.heading: Klan and white business elite
panels.description: A Klan parade photograph is followed by the portrait introduced in narration as Wyatt Tate Brady.
panels.camera: Cut from the parade photograph to a portrait.
panels.action: The marchers are frozen in the still.

panels.heading: Gurley’s reassurance
panels.description: Gurley’s seated portrait returns before a map marks Greenwood, courthouse and armory.
panels.camera: Static portrait, then a cut to a labeled map.

panels.heading: Veterans go to the courthouse
panels.description: The map adds a route from Greenwood to the courthouse; the presenter describes the first armed delegation.
panels.camera: Static map with a route line added.
panels.action: The route line appears on the map.

panels.heading: NRA sarcasm setup
panels.description: An NRA logo cuts to armed Black Panthers on capitol steps, then returns to the logo.
panels.camera: Cuts between the logo and a photograph.
panels.visualGag: The 'remember that time' question sounds approving until 'Oh wait' and the Mulford Act reverse it. The cuts between the NRA logo and the Black Panthers carry both the sarcastic setup and the correction.

panels.heading: Castile callback setup
panels.description: The NRA logo is followed by Philando Castile’s portrait.
panels.camera: Cut from the logo to a portrait.
panels.visualGag: A second 'remember that time' setup repeats the NRA reversal, and the statement-and-tweet image that follows supplies the correction.

panels.heading: Statement contradicted
panels.description: An NRA statement is covered by Dana Loesch’s tweet saying he possessed a controlled substance and firearm simultaneously and ending Stop lying.
panels.camera: Static screenshot with a tweet overlaid.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the Castile setup: the tweet undercuts the statement's universal-rights wording while the narration says devil's lettuce.

panels.heading: Manufacturers and Iran-Contra
panels.description: Gun-manufacturer logos appear; a uniformed Oliver North photograph follows.
panels.camera: Cut from the logos to a photograph.
panels.visualGag: The Oliver North cutaway illustrates 'Iran-Contra veterans' as the narrator dismisses the NRA leadership, and leads into the alternative clubs.

panels.heading: Alternative clubs reveal
panels.description: National African-American Gun Association, Redneck Revolt, Pink Pistols and Socialist Rifle Association logos share the screen.
panels.camera: Static group of logos.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the NRA leadership jab: after the insult, the screen offers named alternatives.

panels.heading: Armory raid rebuffed
panels.description: A brick armory photograph interrupts the city map, then the map returns.
panels.camera: Cut from the map to a photograph and back.

panels.heading: Reconnaissance and second delegation
panels.description: A route line again links Greenwood and the courthouse while the presenter describes the eighty-person contingent and demand for a pistol.
panels.camera: Static map with a route line.
panels.action: The route line links the two sites.

panels.heading: First shots
panels.description: The emblem holds through the account of the first fatal exchange and the pursuit into Greenwood. The violence is described, not animated.
panels.camera: Static emblem on black.

panels.heading: June 1 assault
panels.description: A WEDNESDAY / JUNE 1, 1921 card precedes a night game aerial of burning blocks.
panels.camera: Static date card, then a cut to the night aerial.
panels.action: The fires burn in the game view.

panels.heading: Archer Street burns
panels.description: The model’s commercial buildings glow orange with fire as the view moves over intersections.
panels.camera: The night aerial moves over the burning intersections.
panels.action: Flames and smoke spread through the game buildings and leave blackened shells, illustrating the destruction.

panels.heading: Second assault
panels.description: The night aerial travels across burning shops toward burning residential blocks.
panels.camera: The night aerial travels from the shops toward the houses.
panels.action: Fire spreads from the commercial blocks into the residential streets of the game city.

panels.heading: Historical flames
panels.description: A black-and-white photo shows a building engulfed in smoke and fire, followed by more streets and burning structures.
panels.camera: Cuts between static archival photographs.

panels.heading: Bombing and wider persecution
panels.description: A wide historical photograph of a smoke plume and several street scenes accompany the presenter's account of aircraft and of Black servants detained elsewhere in Tulsa. No plane attack is shown.
panels.camera: Cuts between static archival photographs.

panels.heading: Martial law and detention
panels.description: The game view passes burning houses beside railroad tracks and freight cars.
panels.camera: The game view passes along the railroad.
panels.action: Houses burn beside the tracks and freight cars, leaving blackened ruins.

panels.heading: Casualties
panels.description: A near-overhead view reveals charred blocks and remaining fires while the presenter quotes the commission’s death-toll range.
panels.camera: The aerial rises to a near-overhead view.
panels.action: Remaining fires smolder among the charred game blocks.

panels.heading: Release without justice
panels.description: The devastated model cuts to panoramic historical ruins, then collapsed walls and a ruined street.
panels.camera: Cut from the game model to archival photographs.

panels.heading: Blame and rebuilding
panels.description: An extensive ruins photograph leads into the emblem while the narrator describes the grand jury and residents’ rebuilding plans.
panels.camera: Static photograph, then the emblem.

panels.heading: Winter in tents
panels.description: A tent among debris appears during the fire-code barriers account.
panels.camera: Static archival photograph.

panels.heading: The burned area and depot
panels.description: THE BURNED AREA title is followed by a color photograph of the Union Depot building.
panels.camera: Title card, then a cut to a color photograph.

panels.heading: Recovery loses its circulation
panels.description: The emblem accompanies the presenter’s account of desegregation and suburban shopping draining the local economy.
panels.camera: Static emblem on black.
panels.action: The emblem holds through the explanation.

panels.heading: Disclaimer callback
panels.description: TO BE CLEAR: SEGREGATION IS DUMB AND BAD returns.
panels.camera: Static text card on black.
panels.visualGag: Callback to the earlier disclaimer, again separating an explanation of a perverse economic effect from any endorsement of segregation.

panels.heading: Freeway cuts the neighborhood
panels.description: A static aerial shows the freeway separating the baseball field from campus grounds.
panels.camera: Static aerial photograph.

panels.heading: Reparations recoded
panels.description: The emblem accompanies the presenter’s criticism of reparations recast as economic development, until a brief quoted ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT card cuts in.
panels.camera: Static emblem on black, briefly interrupted by a text card.
panels.action: The text card cuts in, then the emblem returns.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT card in scare quotes, where the benevolent-sounding phrase is decoded as a handout to developers and institutions. The later RESTORED ORDER card uses the same device on another euphemism.

panels.heading: Economic development in scare quotes
panels.description: White quoted ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT text interrupts the DNE emblem on black. The presenter immediately decodes the ostensibly benevolent phrase as a handout to developers and institutions.
panels.camera: Static text card.
panels.action: The text replaces the emblem, which then returns.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the reparations setup: the scare quotes puncture the euphemism while the narration translates it. The later RESTORED ORDER card repeats the device.
panels.notes: In the presenter’s account, the phrase means subsidies to developers and institutions, not reparations paid to residents.

panels.heading: Stadium and campus
panels.description: The ONEOK FIELD entrance photo cuts to a satellite view with the large campus circled.
panels.camera: Cut from a photograph to a satellite view.
panels.action: The campus is circled on the map.

panels.heading: What survives
panels.description: A street-front brick block, Mount Zion church and Vernon chapel appear in succession.
panels.camera: Cuts between static photographs.

panels.heading: House and scattered buildings
panels.description: A red historic house photograph and a multi-story building Street View continue the inventory.
panels.camera: Cut from a photograph to a street view.

panels.heading: Plaques are not a community
panels.description: Ground-level memorial plaques commemorate B. C. Franklin, the Williams Building and another lost site.
panels.camera: Static ground-level photographs.

panels.heading: Class reductionism setup
panels.description: The emblem holds during the narrator’s admission of a knee-jerk class-only analysis.
panels.camera: Static emblem on black.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the /leftypol/ caricature and its explicit rejection. The admission is comic self-criticism, and he drops the class-only view a moment later.

panels.heading: Bad analysis caricature
panels.description: A grinning, top-hatted capitalist caricature labeled /leftypol/ replaces the emblem. Its original source is unknown, and it is not the Monopoly mascot.
panels.camera: Hard cut from the emblem to the image.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the class-reductionism setup: the exaggerated caricature stands for the argument that Greenwood deserved destruction because its residents were class traitors.

panels.heading: Bad analysis rejected
panels.description: White THAT’S A PRETTY BAD ANALYSIS text replaces the caricature.
panels.camera: Static text card on black.
panels.visualGag: The blunt correction completes the /leftypol/ bit, so nobody mistakes the caricature's position for the presenter's.

panels.heading: Black capitalism claim
panels.description: A Stefan Grant tweet reads Socialism is cancer. The only thing that can solve Black poverty is Black Capitalism.
panels.camera: Static screenshot.

panels.heading: Wealth does not guarantee protection
panels.description: The emblem gives way to a Hitler photograph and an Auschwitz gate image during the presenter’s argument about fascism and racist repression.
panels.camera: Cuts from the emblem to two archival photographs.

panels.heading: Malcolm X quotation
panels.description: A photograph of Malcolm X holding a rifle appears beside YOU CAN’T HAVE CAPITALISM WITHOUT RACISM.
panels.camera: Static photograph with a text quotation.

panels.heading: Segregation and class consciousness
panels.description: The segregated drinking-fountain image returns, then the daylight Greenwood reconstruction resumes.
panels.camera: Static photograph, then a cut back to the game aerial.

panels.heading: Community self-defense
panels.description: The reconstruction holds a broad view along the shop-lined avenue while the presenter argues against blaming armed defenders.
panels.camera: Broad aerial along the shop-lined avenue.
panels.action: The view holds over the intact game city while the presenter argues.

panels.heading: Petition and speech counterfactuals
panels.description: A moving aerial passes rail-served industrial buildings and the residential street grid during rhetorical questions about petitioning or inspiring a racist mob.
panels.camera: Moving aerial over the rail-served industry and the residential grid.
panels.action: The camera passes over the intact city; nothing in the scene acts out the questions.

panels.heading: Overwhelming odds
panels.description: The aerial rises toward a more top-down view as the presenter questions the speed of racist organization and the already available bombs.
panels.camera: The aerial rises toward a top-down view.
panels.action: The camera climbs over the intact game city.

panels.heading: A long-made conflict
panels.description: Daylight aerials of the shops and houses continue under the structural explanation, the intact city a reminder of what was lost.
panels.camera: Daylight aerials over the shops and houses.
panels.action: The camera keeps moving over the intact game city.

panels.heading: The state restores order
panels.description: The model cuts away to the emblem, briefly replaced by quoted RESTORED ORDER text.
panels.camera: Cut from the model to the emblem, briefly replaced by a text card.
panels.action: The text card cuts in, then the emblem returns.
panels.visualGag: Bitter scare quotes expose the contradiction the presenter describes: order was restored by arresting the victims. The device repeats the earlier ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT card, used here as dark irony rather than comedy.

panels.heading: When words are not enough
panels.description: The emblem holds while the presenter distinguishes ordinary nonviolent politics from the assault on Greenwood.
panels.camera: Static emblem on black.

panels.heading: Greenwood rebuilt
panels.description: The emblem holds as the presenter says Greenwood recovered and reached its prosperity peak in the 1940s.
panels.camera: Static emblem on black.

panels.heading: Permanent land loss
panels.description: The freeway aerial returns and cuts to the circled campus, tying the final argument to the earlier redevelopment images.
panels.camera: Static aerial, then a cut to the circled campus.

panels.heading: Opportunity to rebuild
panels.description: The circled campus remains before the emblem returns; the presenter says rebuilding requires keeping community resources and usable land.
panels.camera: Static satellite view, then the emblem.

panels.heading: Bonus-series commercial
panels.description: The emblem introduces the monthly one-dollar Patreon pitch and repeats the permission to share unlisted links.
panels.camera: Static emblem on black.
panels.action: The emblem holds through the pitch.

panels.heading: Possible future subjects
panels.description: A Red Vienna housing photograph cuts to a Lower Manhattan Expressway model illustration.
panels.camera: Cut from a photograph to an illustration.

panels.heading: Support and source caveat
panels.description: The emblem accompanies the appeal and the admission that a detailed University of Tulsa timeline was found after completing the episode.
panels.camera: Static emblem on black.

panels.heading: Timeline uncertainty and social signoff
panels.description: The emblem holds while the presenter acknowledges conflicting accounts and jokes that Mastodon is the prehistoric elephant, not Alexander’s homeland.
panels.camera: Static emblem on black.

panels.heading: Credits begin
panels.description: Black transitions to white patron names scrolling vertically.
panels.camera: Fixed black background behind the scrolling names.

panels.heading: Patron credits continue
panels.description: Successive columns of names move upward; the emblem reappears afterward.
panels.camera: Fixed black background behind the scrolling names.
panels.action: Columns of names scroll upward until the emblem returns.

panels.heading: Closing emblem and black
panels.description: The DNE emblem returns and fades to black.
panels.camera: Static emblem on black.
